title: Classes, Objects and Interfaces
introduction: Object-oriented design groups related state and behaviour behind a deliberate public interface.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish a class from an object.
Prefer composition when objects have independent responsibilities.

activities.question: What is an object?
options: A particular instance created from a type or class
activities.explanation: A class describes a form; an object is one instance with its own current state.

activities.question: Encapsulation can protect an object's valid state.
activities.explanation: Controlled operations can enforce rules instead of allowing arbitrary state changes.

activities.question: A car uses an engine with a separate responsibility. Which relationship usually fits?
activities.explanation: Composition builds behaviour from collaborating objects with distinct responsibilities.
